title: Loops inside loops
summary: Put one loop inside another to work with rows and columns.

intro.text:
A loop can sit inside another loop. The **inner loop runs completely for every single round of the outer loop**:

```
for row in range(2):
    for col in range(3):
        print(row, col)
```

That prints 6 lines: for row 0, col goes 0, 1, 2; then for row 1, col goes 0, 1, 2 again. Rounds multiply: 2 times 3 is 6.

Think of the outer loop as **rows** and the inner loop as **columns**. The **grid** panel lights up one cell for every inner round.

To print a row of a pattern, build a string in the inner loop and print it after the inner loop, still inside the outer one. A `break` only leaves the innermost loop it is in.
intro.analogy: A clock: the minute hand goes all the way round, 60 steps, for every single step of the hour hand. The hour hand is the outer loop and the minute hand is the inner loop.

predict.q: What does this print? Type it exactly.
predict.why: For a = 0 the inner loop gives b = 0 and 1. Then for a = 1 it starts again from b = 0.
The inner loop runs 4 times for each of the 3 outer rounds: 3 times 4 is 12.

quiz.q: An outer loop runs 4 times and its inner loop runs 5 times. How many times does the inner block run?
quiz.why: The inner loop runs fully for every outer round: 4 times 5.

quiz.q: When does the inner loop start again from the beginning?
options: At every round of the outer loop
quiz.why: Each outer round runs the whole inner loop again.

quiz.q: A `break` inside the inner loop leaves...
quiz.why: break leaves the innermost loop it is in. The outer loop carries on.

quiz.q: To print one row per outer round, where does the print go?
options: In the outer loop, after the inner loop
quiz.why: After the inner loop has built the row, but still once per outer round.

quiz.q: `for i in range(3):` with an inner `for j in range(i):`. How many inner rounds in total?
Why should the two loops use different variable names?
options: The inner loop would overwrite the outer one's value
quiz.why: The same name would be changed by the inner loop, which is confusing and usually a bug.

mistakes.title: Inner block not indented enough
mistakes.explain: The print should be inside the inner loop, so it needs 8 spaces. With 4 spaces the inner for has no block.

mistakes.title: A loop over a number
